findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_buyer_signals, list_signal_sources, find_buying_intent, get_feedback_reply · Private data: find_buyer_signals, stack_pains, find_buying_intent · Public sink: find_buying_intent, submit_feedback · Destructive: submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_buyer_signals, list_signal_sources, find_buying_intent, get_feedback_reply · Private data: find_buyer_signals, stack_pains, find_buying_intent · Public sink: find_buying_intent, submit_feedback · Destructive: submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "find_buyer_signals" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
